What's to prevent hate groups from subscribing, waiting a month, then flagging the mod for removal? Even if you base it on SCP and CCP they could still do the same by upvote brigading their own content to speed up the process.

They would need a fairly large proportion of the subverse to do it with them, this could be a high % in small subs (eg 75%). Even thousands of brigaders wouldn't be able to cause an issue in a well rooted subverse. Admins could also see mass subscribing of users and void any votes from accounts that come in all at the same time. The idea is that if the vast majority of a sub hates a mod for power abuse they should be able to unseat them.

I agree there should be a process, but no automatic actions. If a vote of no confidence flags a mod, I think an admin should investigate to see if the accusations are factual before taking action. I am not convinced the admins could go back perhaps months to check on subscription frequency though. Maybe they can.

That is utterly surprising, honestly, considering his long history of being a bit of a dickhead. Granted, I'm a bit biased. I did not care at all for his tirade against Cloud Imperium Games and his past attempts at publicity in the past decade have felt like cries for attention rather than carefully thought out examinations of the gaming industry.

His flame war was essentially about one of his earliest projects, Battlecruiser 3000AD, and how badly it sucked. It has continued throughout the ages because many of the projects which Derek works on have failed in significant ways. Either they lack innovation and have decent performance or they lack performance and have decent innovation. The main problem is that he has always blamed other people for the failings of his games. Hell, on more than a few occasions he has blamed his audience. At one point, someone posted a question about BC3kAD saying that they couldn't alt-tab and Dereks' response was that it was a feature and the game demands exclusive access to the computer in order to run. Further responses from Smart and his supporters made it seem as though the player in question was insane to try and alt-tab out of the game considering how great of an accomplishment it was.

More recently, he has produced Alganon which was essentially a poorly done WoW clone, Line of Defence, which is simply horrible to gaze upon, and of course his recent tirade against Star Citizen. Now, I won't sit here and lie to you. I'm a big fan of Star Citizen. However, many people feel that Dereks' multi-blog rant against the game was due to his inability to create a game of similar scope a decade earlier with his Battlecruiser series. In fact, in one of his posts he claimed that a game of such scope was impossible due to the fact that he (Derek Smart) was unable to do it.

Now, regardless of what side you're on here, the thing to take away from this is that Derek doesn't have a great track record for making games. Statistics will show that. He does have an established record for blaming others, getting personally involved in flame wars, and is often times petty with his arguments and retorts. Personally, I find the man despicable and I am shocked to find that he is the rational voice amidst this Gamergate situation. I am old enough to remember his postings on various BBSs in regard to his game so perhaps I am a jaded old fool, a relic of a time long since past. For me, it is to hear that the lead clown is running the circus itself.

However, as always, this is just my two cents on the matter. Take it as you will. I highly recommend reading into the subject matter yourself if you are interested in The Greatest Flame War of All Time.

ADDENDUM: As a follow up, there are quite a few wars which were described as the GoAT. Frankly, I stand by the Derek Smart War of the late 90s as the greatest. You may need to refine your search criteria to find the facts as is a lot of misleading information from both sides.
